Are you familiar with the Skin Effect (or Shielding Effect)? The Skin Effect states that as the frequency of a radiated signal increases, the farther away from the core of an electrical conductor the signal moves. A DC current passed through a wire will pass electrons throughout the entire cross-section of the conductor. There will be moving electrons on the outside of the wire as well as in the very center of the wire. If you increase the frequency of the current flow, the moving electrons start moving away from the center of the conductor and more toward the outside. At very high frequencies, the signal starts to actually "ride" on the very outside of the conductor and not at all in the center. This is why we don't use "wires" to transmit microwave frequencies around different parts of a circuit. Wires are replaced with "waveguides" which are pretty much hollow metal tubes that act like pipes for the signal to move on the outside of (completely unlike water would do).

This Skin Effect is important in determining the danger of high frequency signals. Because the signals want to be on the outside as their frequency increases, the penetration depth of a very high frequency signal becomes less and less. Waves at 60GHz will barely pass into the dead layer of skin cells on your body. 100GHz will pretty much get stopped by that same dead skin. Also, the electrical impedance of your body (both inductive and capacitive) will do interesting things to the signal which can include reflection of the signal or attenuation to a lower strength. You are bombarded by very high frequency EM radiation everyday. The Sun is a very big producer of such signals, as are all other stars and other celestial bodies. This "noise" is a problem for RF engineers. It was also responsible for the discovery of the CMB (Cosmic Microwave Background) that gave rise to the Big Bang Theory of cosmic creation. The amount of very high frequency EM radiation you receive every single second of your life doesn't seem to scare anyone, yet 5G does. I know this field. I know RF/EM electronics. I'm not afraid. Thinking about this more I think I have some of the calculations out of order. Revised below.

In the event of him winning, I would get $23000 + my initial bet of $1000 for a total of $24000. Minus the cut for the bookie at 4.16% is $24000 minus $998.40 for a total of $23001.60. Then I would subtract the lay bet liability of $2088 for a total of $20913.60.

In the event of him losing, I would get $2175 + my initial bet of $87 for a total of $2262. Minus the cut for the bookie at 4% is $2262 minus $90.48 for a total of $2171.52. I would then subtract the back bet of $1000 for a total of $1171.52.

Looking back on the numbers I think I accidentally did the lay bet correctly but just worded it all wrong, but the numbers for the back bet were in the wrong order.

My limited understanding is that, for the lay bet (in the event of him losing), you dont get the payout, you only get the stake.

So if Trump loses, you are not getting $2175 + $87....you are simply getting $87. The $2175 is what you are liable for should you lose the bet.

So to summarize. Lets say

Back odds are 24, stake is $1000

Lay odds are 23, stake is $87

If Trump wins:

- Back earns you $23k (profit) + $1k (initial investment) = $24k minus the 4.16% cut = $23001.6

- Lay loses you liability of $2088 (I believe that includes the 4% owed to the bookie).

Total earnings = $20913

If Trump loses:

- Back loses you $1000 (possibly with the bookie cut, im not sure how they enforce it at your site)

- Lay earns you $87

Total losses = -920

You cant make money off of both him winning and losing....that would be an arbitrage. right now the odds are in favor of him losing, so if you bet against him, you arent winnning as much as you risk to lose if he ends up winning the election.

Hope that makes sense. Read Example 3 in this site for a better explanation https://mybettingsites.co.uk/learn/lay-betting/
